newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Six consortia join the race for Romania GSM tender.
newsitem.headline: Six consortia join the race for Romania GSM tender.

text.p: Romania's Communications Ministry said on Thursday six consortia have joined the race in a tender for two licenses to install and operate a new GSM digital cellular phone network in Romania.
September 26 was deadline for entry to the competition.

The offers lodged by the six consortia including bluTel, MobiFon, MobilRom, Romcell, Telefonica Romania and Zephir would be studied by a ministry commission. Potential winners would be announced after October 25, the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry would also consider plans to hire a foreign consultancy firm to help the commission deal with the evaluation of the offers, it said.

The tender requires companies to be able to cover at least 65 percent of Romania with the GSM system, to have solid operating experience and financial strength to back the costs of the project, expected to cost some $1.0 billion.
The bluTel consortium was formed by Italian telecoms group Stet Spa, Bouygues of France and Britain's Balli Group, backed by investment bank Goldman Sachs.

MobiFon comprises AirTouch Communications Inc of United States, Canada's Telesystem International Wireless. Romania's private Logic Telecom SA, the state-run Posta Romana post authority and ISAF engineering firm are also part of the group.

MobilRom was set up by France Telecom together with Alcatel Network Systems Romania, a local branch of Alcatel, and Romanian private ComputerLand computer retailer and MediaPro media holding. Tomen Telecom Romania a subsidiary of Tomen, is also part of the consortium.
Zephir brings together U.S. Telecoms group Motorola, Danish telecoms Tele Danmark, Norway's Telenor as well as Romania's private Radiotel and Rokura communications operators.
Telefonica Romania, a joint venture between Spain's Telefonica de Espana and the Romanian state telecoms network already operates an analogue mobile system on the 450 Mhz waveband in the country.

Last week, it threatened to sue the Romanian government to block it from holding the tender. Telefonica's argument is that it was promised the right to operate digital GSM services in 1992 when it began to offer its service and it therefore considers it is already licensed to provide GSM services.
The communications ministry rejected the claims as groundless.
On Thursday, Telefonica Romania said it had submitted its offer for the bid because it wished "to cooperate with the Romanian government for the development of the communications."
However its offer did not imply "a renunciation to the right which it has for one of the two licences," Telefonica Romana said in a statement.
Data on Romcell consortium was not available on Thursday.
With a population of 23 million people and relatively few landlines the telecoms ministry says the potential market for digital mobile phones is huge. -- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
